items.title: Aleph Alpha shipped a sovereign open model
items.oneliner: Aleph Alpha launched 78B Kolibri with 1M-token context and on-prem deployment, making EU-compliant enterprise AI more credible.

items.title: Stratego finally fell to AI
items.oneliner: Ataraxos beat Stratego legend Pim Niemeijer 15-2, showing hidden-information planning is no longer an AI blind spot.

items.title: Local inference got more practical
items.oneliner: DwarfStar 4 targets Apple Silicon and CUDA boxes, pushing DeepSeek-class local inference closer to serious developer workflows.

items.title: A court rejected AI victim testimony
items.oneliner: An Arizona appeals court tossed a sentence over an AI-generated victim video, drawing a hard line on synthetic evidence.

items.title: Utah's VPN law hit reality
items.oneliner: A court agreed Utah demanded the technically impossible from VPNs, a rare ruling where privacy engineering beat political theater.

items.title: Apple tightened full disk access
items.oneliner: Apple will require clearer user consent for Full Disk Access, closing a permission path that quietly exposed sensitive local data.

items.title: Cloudflare productized private HTTP routing
items.oneliner: Cloudflare launched an OHTTP Gateway, giving developers a cleaner way to hide user IPs without forcing VPN-style tradeoffs.

items.title: Coding agents got a shared workspace
items.oneliner: Offrun puts multiple coding agents in isolated git worktrees, which is exactly the orchestration layer agent-heavy teams need.

items.title: A cloud-native operating system emerged
items.oneliner: FTL proposes a userspace cloud OS with stronger container isolation, hinting that Linux may not be the final abstraction.

items.title: Kagi abandoned Orion beyond Apple platforms
items.oneliner: Kagi stopped Orion development for Linux and Windows and open-sourced both, a reminder that cross-platform browsers are brutally expensive.
